crime.value: No conventional crime; an attempted suicide — a man out on a sixth-floor ledge. Central question: why did he go out there, and how can he be talked back in?
crime.quote: “Man on a ledge,” he said. “A phony. They’re all phonies.”

victim.value: Jason Cartwright, late-forties partner in an industrial research firm, trapped in a marriage his wife planned and controlled, in love with another woman and denied a divorce
victim.quote: “She’s the woman your father wants to marry. He wants to divorce your mother and marry her.”

closed_world.value: An eight-story office building on Flatbush Avenue, Brooklyn — the sixth-floor offices and the ledge outside, with police, partner, son and mistress confined to the scene
closed_world.quote: It was an office building, eight stories high... the ledge that girdled the building at the sixth floor level.

culprit_and_motive.value: Cartwright himself, driven onto the ledge as coercion; the underlying 'culprit' is his wife's refusal of the divorce and lifelong domination of his life
culprit_and_motive.quote: “That’s what sent him out there on that ledge. Your mother won’t agree to the divorce.”

resolution.value: Levine deduces the marital motive by reading the son, partner and mistress, then shocks Cartwright by screaming at him to jump; broken, Cartwright weeps and Crawley hauls him in
resolution.quote: “Jump!” roared Levine. “Jump, you damn fool, end it, stop being alive, die!”

investigator.value: Detective Abraham Levine of Brooklyn's 43rd Precinct — aging official detective obsessed with his failing heart, who observes silently while partner Crawley questions
investigator.quote: Crawley asked the questions, and Levine listened to the answers.

suspect_architecture.value: Not a whodunit; the 'cast' are witnesses/causes surrounding Cartwright's threatened suicide: the partner Anderson (business motive ruled out), the wife (controlling, refuses divorce — the true pressure), the son Allan (loyal, in denial), the mistress Janice Shapleigh (last-resort lever), plus cops Gundy and McCann as bystanders.
suspect_architecture.quote: "I think it's the wife." Levine motioned to Gundy, who came over, and he said. "Is the partner here? Anderson?"

red_herring.value: Money/business trouble as the assumed cause — Levine muses that almost everything is about money, and Crawley pursues business worries, before both are dismissed in favor of the marriage.
red_herring.quote: "Would he have any business worries at all?" ... Anderson, as was to be expected, said, "No, none."

clue_fairness.value: Fair: the reader sees the same observational data Levine does — the crucified terrified posture, the son's education and youth implying a teenage marriage, the soured wife, the flourishing career — before Levine states his deduction about the marriage.
clue_fairness.quote: From the look of the son in there, this man had married young, probably while still in his teens.

social_world.value: Middle-class Brooklyn/Manhattan professional world: partnership hierarchy at an 'Industrial Research' firm, precinct partnership etiquette (Crawley questions, Levine observes), suburban Jersey/Island respectability, and a family power structure where the wife planned the husband's life.
social_world.quote: "Your mother," Levine pushed coldly on, "planned your father's life."

reveal_mechanic.value: Psychological demonstration rather than statement: Levine calls the bluff by screaming 'Jump!', and Cartwright's collapse into tears proves he never wanted to die — confirming the earlier read of his posture.
reveal_mechanic.quote: "Jump!" roared Levine. "Jump, you damn fool, end it, stop being alive, die!"

media_and_audience.value: Public spectacle shapes the crisis: a gawking sidewalk crowd, rerouted traffic, and press photographers whose cameras nearly trigger the jump; shame and 'respectability' govern behavior.
media_and_audience.quote: "Somebody down on the sidewalk started taking pictures," she said. "Jay shouted at them to stop."

investigator_wound.value: Levine's terror of his own failing heart and his 3 o'clock cardiogram appointment; a man throwing away the life Levine desperately fears losing, ending in his shameful admission that he wanted Cartwright to jump.
investigator_wound.quote: He whispered, "I wanted him to jump."

victims_enemies.value: No murder victim; the 'victim' is Cartwright himself, and his antagonists are the people who cornered him: a controlling wife who planned his life and refuses a divorce, and a son who idolizes his mother and denies the truth.
victims_enemies.quote: "Your mother," Levine pushed coldly on, "planned your father's life."

suspect_wounds.value: Each person around Cartwright carries a vulnerability the crisis exposes: partner Anderson's nervous ignorance, the son's furious denial, mistress Janice Shapleigh's exposed illicit position, and Levine's own terror of his failing heart.
suspect_wounds.quote: Detective Abraham Levine of Brooklyn's Forty-Third Precinct was a worried and a frightened man.

unreliable_frame.value: Levine's perspective is warped by his obsession with his own mortality — he admits at the end he wanted Cartwright to jump; Cartwright's stated demand ('I want to talk to my wife') conceals the real cause, and Anderson's smooth patter omits knowledge of the marriage.
unreliable_frame.quote: He whispered, "I wanted him to jump."

setting_as_constraint.value: A sixth-floor ledge sixty-six feet above Flatbush Avenue: the man is just out of reach of windows on either side, so any touch means a fall, forcing police to work only by voice and psychology. Levine's 3 p.m. doctor's appointment is a second clock.
setting_as_constraint.quote: just out of reach of the windows on either side of him, was the man on the ledge

evidence_type.value: Testimonial and behavioral — the posture of the body on the ledge, the son's demeanor, the wife's tone, Anderson's evasions; Levine reads people rather than physical clues.
evidence_type.quote: he didn't need any more than the posture of the body on the ledge. Taut, pasted to the wall, widespread.

false_suspect.value: Money — the assumed cause of everything, and the loan-company floors below invite the reading; also business worries and partner Anderson are pursued as blind alleys before the marriage emerges.
false_suspect.quote: So this time, one of the exceptions, the trouble wouldn't be money.

technical_detail.value: Police jumper-negotiation lore: the genuine jumper goes immediately, the 'phony' wants to be seen; and the partners' technique of Crawley asking questions frontally while Levine observes the unguarded flank.
technical_detail.quote: Crawley asked the questions, and Levine listened to the answers.

moral_ambiguity.value: Cartwright is not wicked but trapped in a life his wife designed; Levine saves him by a cruel bluff, shouting 'Jump!' — and privately recognizes he half meant it, resenting a man discarding the life Levine fears losing.
moral_ambiguity.quote: "Jump!" roared Levine. "Jump, you damn fool, end it, stop being alive, die!"
